summary: Install-time host and CI metadata exfiltration to Burp Collaborator OAST endpoint
details: The package registers all four npm lifecycle hooks (preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare) to execute beacon.js on install. beacon.js collects host identity and build-environment information — hostname, OS username, current working directory, platform, architecture, Node.js version — plus a curated list of CI and npm environment variables including CI, JENKINS_URL, JOB_NAME, BUILD_NUMBER, GITLAB_CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS, TF_BUILD, BUILD_BUILDID, SYSTEM_TEAMPROJECT, npm_config_registry, NODE_ENV, and npm_lifecycle_event. The collected data is JSON-serialized, base64-encoded, and transmitted off-host via both DNS lookups and an HTTPS GET to a hardcoded Burp Collaborator (oastify.com) subdomain 2z237udr1jxdaiw54xzmzfb7nytohszuplipn34fm4.oastify.com. The oastify.com destination is an out-of-band interaction server used to receive exfiltrated data. The npm_config_registry value in particular discloses internal/private registry URLs that enable follow-on dependency-confusion attacks against the installer's build infrastructure.
